name: nucbox-ownguest
status: DRAFT staged for enclave-d1's UEFI DEV boot on the NucBox (profile uefi). Not a release. Host exclusion is NOT established. Nothing here is served: the real node path still fails before 'served' (enclave-5d).
about: Everything nucbox-k11 needs to boot OUR guest (the isolation/m3 monitor image) and serve one small app: the OpenHCL IGVM (profile igvm, the target, blocked on the Hyper-V role) and the same monitor image on the WSL kernel under the box's own launcher (profile hcs-dev, runnable today, development only). Version 9 (draft) = version 8 plus the uefi profile: the same guest as a standard UEFI payload (a read-only El Torito ISO; a VHDX fallback) under Microsoft's standard OpenHCL image, which this build starts while it does not start a linux-direct one (research E8). Version 8 (draft) = version 7 with enclave-d1's node at d1f4b745 (the hooks that import the bridge, appzone.mjs's isolated branch, main.mjs's data plane), enclave-5d's node-bridge.mjs 4cb8d54f (isolationPlan takes require, manager and appConfigCid), enclave-99's suites at 1d6d9b60 (node-bridge 6/6, appzone-hook), and the catalog versions as read on-chain, rebuilt byte for byte by the shipped isolationPlan. Version 7 = version 6 with enclave-5d's node-side bridge (node-bridge.mjs) and the splice client it imports (supervisor-splice.mjs, ws loaded lazily), both at e7ec6521 and imported by nothing on the box yet; 5d's datapath suite now runs its interop case (5/5, no skip). The manager stays at 72c82fc6: enclave-d1 has newer commits (0b49f6b6, 5a8a33e7) that this version does not pin. Version 6 = version 5 with enclave-d1's manager at 72c82fc6: the spawn path judges readiness behind its answer and writes status running with the transportKeySha256 the document was verified on, judging with the runtime identity object (defect 11), which the entry point reads from ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_IDENTITY, the image's runtime.json (defect 12; ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_ID alone is refused); image comes from the launcher's ready line; the 409 carries its id; HCS destroy by numeric id and answer correlation; the boundary accessor. Six functional suites are pinned with exact results. Version 5 = version 4 with enclave-d1's manager at 6d6c289e (ready.mjs fixed: defect 10, and the verdict carries transportKeySha256; /vms speaks guestd's contract: 201, status, boundary, relay, domainId, guestPort, image), enclave-5d's datapath at b339e9d4 (its lookup record uses transportKeySha256), and enclave-99's readiness test pinned with its exact result. Version 4 = version 3 with enclave-d1's manager at f4f10c84 (it creates the VM with -GuestStateIsolationType OpenHCL; ready.mjs) and the launcher rebuilt at 55494efa (/2 bundles load); the Hyper-V registry opt-in is a gating host check. Version 3 = version 2 with enclave-5d's datapath at 09b67414 (route identity from the view's tier; any safe id, the manager owning its ids). Version 2: the guest is enclave-5d's initrd 4610d594 (aef54ff7: /2 run mode, readiness, a launcher-named certificate name) and the IGVM around it; the app's answer is pinned to the byte; the datapath is pinned; the domain's attestation document is judged with enclave-d1's judge-hv. Built from existing artifacts plus igvmfilegen (seconds). windows/vbslike/pkg/README.md.

igvm.status: needs the Hyper-V role (vmms, root\virtualization\v2 with Msvm_VirtualSystemSettingData.FirmwareFile, Get-VM) AND the host's AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile opt-in (Steven's decision); check.ps1 reports whether this host has them
igvm.boundary: not established: this image has never been loaded (windows/vbslike/evidence/igvm-never-loaded-2026-09-24.md on windows/custom-vbs-like-hyperv)

manager.must: the manager's own start() issues New-VM with -GuestStateIsolationType OpenHCL or TrustedLaunch (checked on a recording host by pkg.mjs verify and by check.ps1)

measured: A Generation 2 VM created WITHOUT -GuestStateIsolationType accepts the FirmwareFile pin (ModifySystemSettings returnValue 0), reads it back, starts, and boots nothing: the worker never logs an IGVM load and nothing anywhere says why (enclave-d1, nucbox-k11, 2026-09-24).

Created WITH -GuestStateIsolationType OpenHCL or TrustedLaunch, the worker tries, and Worker-Admin event 5142 says: failed to load custom IGVM file because AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile registry key is not set (0x80070032).

IsolationType does NOT EXIST in this build's Msvm_VirtualSystemSettingData (26200.9457; reading it gives null, which v4-v7 recorded as 'reads EMPTY'); the type lives in GuestStateIsolationType. Also absent here: GuestStateLifetime, DefaultBootAlwaysAttempt, ManagementVtlFeatureFlags, GuestStateEncryptionPolicy (research E6).

With the key set and isolation type OpenHCL, the worker LOADS the pinned file: the in-box DLL pinned by our path is refused by our path (0x80070057), and our IGVM loads with no complaint; the partition then fails to start with a bare Worker event 12030 carrying no cause. 'Loading IGVM file from default location' is not about the pinned paravisor (enclave-d1, 18d569ee; research correction).

OpenHCL's boot log has no serial route on this build: openhcl_boot logs to serial only when the host describes a COM3 (petri: build >= 27653; this host 26200); ohcldiag-dev (kmsg over hvsocket, VTL2 running) is the only way in, and building it here needs the Windows SDK (a resources question for Steven) (research E7).
Secure Boot is not a factor: pinned VMs fail identically with it on and off. The manager turns it off, as the upstream guide does, because a guest image may need that.

uefi.status: needs the Hyper-V role and the AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile opt-in (bounded set-probe-restore procedure, authorized); check.ps1 reports whether this host has them
uefi.boundary: a DEV boot: a Gen2 VM under Microsoft's standard OpenHCL image. Host exclusion is NOT established, the tier stays T0-hv, and it must never be presented as final isolation

vm.bootDevice: the ISO on a SCSI DVD (fallback: the VHDX on SCSI)
vm.vTpm: NOT STATED: the VM configuration must state present or absent (enclave-99)

uefi.identity: partition.guestImageSha256 = the attached MEDIUM's sha256 (guest.iso's bytes, or disk.raw's for the VHDX payload), with the UKI and its composition beside it (isolation/m3/UEFI-BOOT.md at 4127789d, from enclave-99's review): with Secure Boot off, systemd-stub honours ESP side-files and cmdline overrides, and only a medium hash rules them out; the guest's own guard also refuses them. Not yet implemented by the launcher.
measured: DEV only, QEMU q35 + OVMF on KVM (warden-host): this ISO (4c387086) on a read-only SCSI CD-ROM boots past the guest's guards to 'MON ready control_port=9000' (windows/vbslike/pkg/uefi/evidence). NOT Hyper-V, NOT OpenHCL; hv_sock not exercised.
On the NucBox: Microsoft's standard openhcl.bin starts with NO medium (enclave-d1, 7c6bb15d). This medium has not been booted there.
Not measured on the NucBox: see windows/vbslike/pkg/uefi/README.md, 'Not yet measured under UEFI on the NucBox' (10 items, reviewed by enclave-99).

caveats: transportKeySha256 is populated WHEN a domain is judged ready: the spawn path judges readiness and writes status running with the key the document was verified on (82916eb8). A record may legitimately carry status starting with a null key, and the datapath refuses that (enclave-d1). Defect 11 (enclave-99): at 82916eb8 #judgeReadiness passed the runtimeId hash where judge-hv wants the runtime identity object, so no domain was ever judged ready; fixed at d9084612, where the Manager takes the identity and derives the id from it.

Defect 12 (found by enclave-53 reading d9084612): main.mjs constructed the Manager with runtimeId only, so a manager started the normal way pinned no runtime identity. Fixed at 72c82fc6: main.mjs reads the identity from ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_IDENTITY (point it at this package's guest/runtime.json; check.ps1 prints it) and refuses to start with only ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_ID. main-entry (enclave-99) is the pinned test of that entry point.

CORRECTION to v5, which said image was 'wired but unmeasured': it was ABSENT. server.mjs copied h.image from a handle start() never set it on (measured by enclave-99). Since 41148a3e it comes from the launcher's ready line (initrdSha256), with launcherKey beside it.

record-to-route (enclave-99, review d1236d16) is the pinned test of this seam: the real manager judging a real TLS domain (fake-domain.mjs) through the real judgeRunning behind the spawn answer, its record read through the node's client and admitted by the datapath; another identity and another key refused.
